Three small things went out this week, and none of them made a headline.

Our sign-up page loads in under a second now. Search finds a page by its title even with a typo. And new teams get a short tour instead of an empty screen.

None of it is flashy. All of it is what people asked us for in September.

Thank you to Noa and Dan, who did the hard parts.

title: The one hiring question I keep
status: draft
created: 2026-10-16
---
I hired four people this year. One question told me more than all the others:

"What did you change your mind about in the last year?"

The best answers were small and specific. A tool they stopped using. A habit they picked up. A belief about their own work that turned out to be wrong.

People who can name one are people who keep learning.

---
title: We stopped doing design reviews in meetings
status: draft
created: 2026-10-14
audience: everyone
---
We stopped holding design reviews in meetings.

Now a designer posts three screens and one question in a shared page by Tuesday. Everyone answers in writing by Thursday.

Fewer opinions, better ones, and nobody waits a week for a slot.

One year ago I became a team lead. Three things I would tell myself on day one:

1. Write things down. Your team reads more than it hears.
2. Say no early, and say why.
3. Your calendar is the plan. Guard the mornings.
